stem: A 10-year-old boy with ADHD returns 3 weeks after starting stimulant treatment and now eats very little at school but has a better evening appetite; which adverse effect best fits this pattern?

options.text: Loss of appetite, especially at lunch
Hypertension as the most common adverse effect

explanation: Loss of appetite, especially at lunch, is the best fit. Stimulant medicines commonly suppress appetite during the school day, with appetite often improving later in the evening.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 85

rationale: Stimulants commonly reduce appetite, particularly around lunchtime, so a child who eats little at school but better at night is showing a typical adverse effect.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because stimulant treatment commonly causes appetite suppression, especially at lunchtime, with later evening appetite often returning.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because hearing impairment is not a typical adverse effect of stimulant treatment for ADHD.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because hypertension can occur and should be monitored, but it is not the most common adverse effect described here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because intellectual disability is not a stimulant adverse effect and does not explain the change in appetite pattern.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because night sweats are not the characteristic adverse effect of stimulant treatment in this scenario.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
